title: Wandering in the CKS Memorial Hall
store: CKS Memorial Hall Museum Gift Shop
description: Pastel painting capturing the grand architecture of the National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall with its blue octogonal roof, white marble walls and tiered base, viewed from the surrounding gardens with a lotus pond framing the foreground. Titled "Early Summer at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall" (初夏的中正紀念堂) by the Taiwanese artist Chang Zhe-xiong (張哲雄).
history: Following the death of President Chiang Kai-shek in 1975, architect Yang Cho-cheng designed this landmark which opened to the public on April 5, 1980. Over the decades, its massive front courtyard—now called Liberty Square—has evolved from an authoritarian monument into the vibrant epicenter of Taiwan's modern democratic gatherings and civil protests. The artwork depicted in the postcard is preserved in the Taiwan Cultural Memory Bank.
note: The back says: 'Spreading the Fragrance of Flowers and Plants, Enriching the Growth of Heaven and Earth. Each encounter weaves together moments of tenderness and longing, one by one'. To my disappointment, it was raining the day I visited and seeing how goergous the colours look during the summer, I made a promise to myself that I would come back to chase the sunnier weather.

title: Snack Price List
store: 來好 LAI HAO 凱撒二店
description: Vintage Taiwanese advertisement features six panels arranged in a grid, showcasing retro summer refreshments. The top row displays a green glass bottle of HeySong Soda, a classic bottle of Coca-Cola on ice, and a colorful tin of grape juice. The bottom row includes a paper cup of ice cream, a packaged chocolate ice pop, and simple green and pink popsicles, accompanied by vertical Chinese text and historical prices
history: This menu illustrates the mid-20th-century consumer landscape in Taiwan, where local staples met expanding Western influences. Homegrown brands represented deep-rooted tradition, while the presence of Coca-Cola highlights the post-war arrival of multinational corporations. The shift toward mass-produced ice cream cups and wrapped popsicles reflects the rise of commercial refrigeration and a booming modern snack culture.
note: Tawainese food might be one of my favourite cusines, and there is something so conforming in retro branding designs. so colourful and honest.

title: Potasse d'Alsace
description: Oval-shaped vintage ad with a royal blue background and bold white text at the bottom reading "POTASSE D'ALSACE". In the center, a white stork with a black wing and red legs stands on one foot. The lower background features a black silhouette of a city skyline, with the sharp spire of a gothic cathedral.
history: This iconic artwork was designed in 1929 by the famous Alsacian illustrator Hansi, as a marketing campaign for the regional potassium mines. It was widely distributed across Europe and North America as promotional postcards, posters, and enamel signs to market Alsacian potash as a premium agricultural fertilizer. Today, the imagery is highly celebrated both as a symbol of Alsacian cultural heritage and as a valuable collector's item in vintage advertising.

title: Straatsoper, Wien
description: Solid black background with the word "WIEN" written across the bottom half in large, elongated, orange-brown block letters. The top half showcases a circular illustration of the grand, illuminated facade of the Vienna State Opera house. In front of the building, a bustling crowd is artistically represented by a vibrant mosaic of hundreds of small, multicolored dots that simulate late-19th to early-20th-century formal attire.
history: This image belongs to the highly sought-after artistic postcards produced during the Vienna Secession and Wiener Werkstätte movements around 1900–1910. Graphic designers and artists of this era created these cards to democratize modern art, transforming everyday tourist souvenirs into collectible, high-design masterpieces. The styling perfectly captures the affluent, avant-garde Fin de Siècle atmosphere of Vienna's golden cultural age.
note: My prized possession, I find this postcard so creatively charming for no reason, I spent no more than 2 hours in the city the first time I visited Vienna and 20 minutes were spent exploring the store I bought this at. I haven't been able to find who made it, but I will.

title: Pastel de nata
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte
description: Detailed color drawing of four Portuguese egg tarts (pastéis de nata) clustered tightly together. The tarts have a golden, flaky puff pastry crust and custard centers featuring distinct dark, caramelized blisters. On the left side of the tarts, the Portuguese words "Pastel de nata" are written in an elegant, handwritten cursive font, accompanied vertically by bold Chinese characters reading "澳門葡萄撻" (Macau Portuguese Tart)
history: The Portuguese egg tart is a defining culinary symbol of Macau's unique, centuries-old Sino-Portuguese fusion culture. Originally inspired by traditional conventual sweets from Lisbon monasteries, the recipe was modified locally in Macau during the late 20th century to create a distinctly creamier, less sweet version. Today, this globally famous pastry represents how colonial heritage seamlessly blended with Cantonese preferences, making it a proud icon of Macau's identity and street food scene.
note: Pastéis de nata taste diferent around the world, macanese egg tarts are not as sweet and obvisouly i'm a little biased towards the originals, but how fun to travel to the other side of the world and get to have a piece of home with you.

title: Ginja de Portugal
description: Vintage pale-green Portuguese liquor label featuring a diagonal white banner with bold red letters reading "GINJA DE PORTUGAL." A branch of vibrant red sour cherries drops over a pink ribbon marked "LICOR SUPERFINO," next to two gold medals and the royal coat of arms. The bottom displays an illustration of Lisbon's historic Belém Tower on the water, alongside a pink circular stamp showing a red anchor for "FABRICA ANCORA."
history: Fábrica Âncora, an iconic Lisbon distillery founded in 1882 that eventually became the official supplier to the Portuguese royal family. Ginjinha is a beloved traditional sour cherry liqueur that stands as Lisbon's most iconic regional drink. By pairing the historic Belém Tower with international gold medals, the label reflects the national pride and global ambitions of 19th-century Portuguese craftsmanship.
note: Bought at one of my favourite places in lisbon that no longer exists.

title: Evzones
description: Group of four Greek soldiers (Evzones) marching in perfect synchronization across a paved stone courtyard. They are dressed in their historic ceremonial military uniforms, featuring white plisséd skirts, long stockings, and hats with hanging black tassels. In the background, Greek text is engraved directly into the large cream-colored stone blocks of the monument wall.
history: The Evzones (or Tsoliades) are part of the elite Presidential Guard unit of the Greek Army. Founded officially in 1868 as a crack light infantry unit, they served with great distinction in major conflicts like the Balkan Wars and World War I. Today, their role is purely ceremonial, but they remain powerful symbols of national pride, military valor, and historical struggle. Published by Editions Sotiris Toumbis.
note: I find the composition of this quite intriguing it's unusual, a little off since every subject is turned away from the viewers perpective. It reminds me of something out of a photography book.

title: Edelweiss
description: Vintage-style botanical illustration featuring several white edelweiss flowers with velvety petals and yellow centers in the foreground. In the background, a majestic, snow-dusted alpine mountain peak rises against a muted, earthy-toned sky. The bottom of the artwork includes elegant cursive script and French text identifying the scenic location.
history: Edelweiss is a deeply cherished emblem of Swiss and Austrian national identity, frequently used by elite alpine military units to represent rugged resilience. Its immense popularity during the 19th-century alpine tourism boom led to over-picking, making it one of the first plants in the world to be legally protected. The postcard artwork is by Catherine Ernst, a contemporary Swiss botanical illustrator and painter known for her detailed depictions of alpine flora.ns.
note: My first postcard ever! from a free weekend when i was interning in Meyrin at 18 years old, what a time. If only she knew it would be the first of many. in a way I'm sure she did,

title: Future
description: Colorful, highly detailed contemporary tapestry featuring two men standing side-by-side in white and light pink suits overlayed with molecular and abstract line drawings. They are surrounded by an intricate background packed with psychedelic patterns, scientific diagrams, circuitry motifs, and royal coats of arms in the four corners.
history: Titled "Fremtiden" (The Future), this piece is part of a series of 17 modern tapestries designed by Danish artist Bjørn Nørgaard and woven by Manufacture des Gobelins as a 50th birthday gift for Queen Margrethe II of Denmark. It hangs in Christiansborg Palace and depicts her two sons—the current King Frederik X and Prince Joachim—surrounded by technological and biological motifs to symbolize the future of the nation and its monarchy.
note: Absolutely loved the tapestries, this one was my favourite. Maybe because it looks towards the future rather than depict past events. Not a postcard but a greeting card, but I couldn't not bring a bit of the art with me.

title: Injured Bridge
description: Folk-art style painting depicts a winter cityscape featuring a massive terracota archway and a right-side cliffside dripping with red, blood-like streaks. Tiny stylized figures walk across the snowy ground and winding paths amidst bare trees, with red-roofed buildings and distant twin cathedral spires lining the horizon.
history: Painted in 1941 by Czech artist Karel Otto Hrubý during the Nazi occupation of Czechoslovakia, this artwork is titled "Krvácující most" (The Injured Bridge). The surreal imagery of blood pouring from the city's structures serves as a powerful wartime allegory for the violence, suffering, and political oppression experienced by the population.
note: One of my personal favourites, I find disturbing imagery fascinating and it made me wonder what surreal representation of a more dark event this could be, as I was oblivious of its history at the time.

title: Tokei (Tokyo): Hiroo and Roppongi
description: Bird's-eye-view illustration shows a modern Tokyo cityscape featuring the Roppongi Hills tower surrounded by dense urban housing. Floating, scalloped golden clouds slice through the landscape, creating a stark contrast against the muted greys and whites of the buildings.
history: Created by contemporary artist Akira Yamaguchi, this artwork utilizes the traditional Yamato-e and Ukiyo-e styles to comment on Japan's rapid post-war modernization. By superimposing historical artistic conventions—like golden mist and bird's-eye perspective—onto 21st-century infrastructure, it explores the tension between cultural heritage and urban development. The inclusion of samurai-era architecture alongside modern skyscrapers highlights the layers of history coexisting within modern Tokyo.

title: My Neighbour Totoro
description: Soft watercolor illustration by Hayao Miyazaki showing the character Mei in winter clothes looking up at a large Totoro covered in snow, with the Japanese text わたしはだれだ…？ (Who am I...?) written below.
history: Created during the early concept stages of the 1988 Studio Ghibli masterpiece My Neighbor Totoro, this artwork reflects Miyazaki's unique pre-production design process and soft artistic style. Over the decades, it has become a beloved piece of Ghibli merchandise, appearing on official seasonal stationery and packaging for the famous Shiro-Hige's Totoro Cream Puff Shop in Tokyo.

title: A Pint of Sheep
description: Graphic illustration of a stylized pint glass filled with curly-textured black sheep representing the dark stout beer, topped with a thick head of white-wooled sheep acting as the foam, all set against a black background with the title "A Pint of Sheep" at the top.
history: Created as a popular contemporary Irish souvenir design, this artwork playfully combines two of Ireland's most famous cultural icons: its rural abundance of sheep and its world-renowned dark stout beer (Guinness). It serves as a humorous visual pun tailored for the tourism market, celebrating Irish identity and wit through a clever pop-art graphic.

title: Date Night
description: A surreal corner room with vibrant red walls where a large, pink-skinned arm reaches from the right to lift a businessman in a blue suit with chopsticks. In the foreground, a giant black bowl is filled with yellow ramen noodles and a hard-boiled egg next to a small green bowl holding a pair of legs and a red rose, while a third figure falls upside down onto the noodles beneath a small yellow fire emblem on the wall.
history: Created in 2021 by the contemporary Indian artist and creative director Sargam Gupta, this artwork belongs to a series exploring themes of modern romance, routine, and emotional surrealism. The visual metaphor flips the dynamics of a typical dinner setting into an existential playground, using bold pop-art textures, high-contrast primary colors, and playful distortions to comment on the consumerist nature and overwhelming sensory experiences of contemporary human dating and relationships.

title: Utopies Bruxelloises
description: This artwork depicts a dense, futuristic metropolis rising directly behind traditional European-style houses with red-tiled roofs. High-overhead elevated highways and multi-tiered skyways cross between soaring, pale golden skyscrapers and sphere-like structures, while sleek aircraft zoom through a warm, reddish-orange sky.
history: This illustration is by renowned French artist François Schuiten, taken from his acclaimed graphic novel series Les Cités Obscures (The Obscure Cities) created with writer Benoît Peeters. The image draws heavy inspiration from Retro-Futurism and 19th-century architecture, particularly reflecting the historical concept of "Brusselization"—the rapid, controversial introduction of modern high-rises into historic urban areas in post-WWII Brussels.

title: Naval Flag of the Chinese Republic
store: 來好 LAI HAO 凱撒二店

title: Then the Tabby went far, and farther than far
description: monochrome, vintage-style pencil and charcoal illustration depicting a large, wide-eyed tabby cat walking forward along a dirt pathway. The cat's body is hunched forward in an intense, menacing posture, with its tail raised high and its mouth open to expose sharp, prominent teeth. It features prominent dark stripes across its fur and ears drawn back, emerging from a softly rendered, textured background of forest foliage and trees.
history: This artwork is a famous 1906 drawing titled "Så gikk kjetta langt og lenger enn langt" ("Then the Tabby went far, and farther than far") by the celebrated Norwegian artist Theodor Kittelsen. It was created as a folklore illustration for the popular Norwegian fairy tale "The Tabby who was such a Glutton" (Kjetta som var saa gammel til å ete), published in collections by Peter Christen Asbjørnsen and Jørgen Moe. Kittelsen is highly regarded in Norway for his atmospheric and sometimes unsettling depictions of nature, fairy tales, and mythical trolls.
note: I like to image the cat gets bigger every step it takes.

title: Constantinople, the Top-Kahné Mosque
description: Oil painting capturing a serene waterfront scene bathed in glowing, atmospheric blue and gold light at dusk or dawn. In the foreground, figures navigate a small wooden rowboat across softly rippling waters toward a grand mosque featuring a central dome, illuminated arches, and two towering minarets along the shoreline.
history: This artwork is by the Russian-Armenian Romantic painter Ivan Aivazovsky, celebrated for his dramatic atmospheric vistas and marine landscapes. The scene depicts 19th-century Constantinople (present-day Istanbul) along the Bosporus, capturing the city's iconic Ottoman architecture through the European Orientalist fascination with the beauty and light of the East.

title: casino
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte

title: Kitten mascot of the aircraft carrier HMS Eagle
description: Black-and-white photograph shows a small, striped tabby cat resting comfortably in a miniature, custom-made canvas hammock complete with tiny pillows. The hammock is suspended indoors against a metallic, industrial backdrop, featuring a large oval hatch or bulkhead door in the background
history: This famous photograph from the Imperial War Museum archives captures "Unsinkable Sam" (or similar ship's mascot, famously known as Convoy, the ship's cat aboard HMS Hermes in 1941). Ships' cats were a longstanding naval tradition across military and merchant vessels, kept both for practical pest control and as beloved mascots to boost crew morale during World War II.

title: Taipei Chifeng Street Alleyway
description: Watercolor-and-ink illustration of a narrow alley between tall, weathered apartment buildings under a bright blue sky. An orange awning shades a shopfront on the left, a streetlamp arches over the lane on the right, and bicycles and scooters line the street. Yellow crisscross lines are painted on the foreground pavement.
history: Chifeng Street in Taipei's Datong District is an older neighborhood known for its narrow lanes, workshops, and local shops, and in recent years it has also become a hub for cafés and creative businesses. The illustration captures that balance between traditional daily life and urban renewal, a common theme in the "urban sketching" movement.

title: art deco
description: An Art Nouveau poster of a woman with long, dark, flowing hair adorned with red flowers, reclining in a pale orange-yellow gown. She holds a lit cigarette in one raised hand and a small JOB packet in the other. A large green circle frames her, with big brown "JOB" lettering across the top and a yellow geometric pattern behind.
history: Designed by Czech artist Alphonse Mucha in 1898, this lithograph was a commercial advertisement for the French JOB cigarette paper company [JOB Collection]. It defines the Art Nouveau movement's trend of blending fine art with mass advertising to sell products through stylized, sensory imagery. The woman's cascading, swirling hair became a hallmark of the Belle Époque design aesthetic.

title: The Smile of the Alberta Sphinx
description: Whimsical illustration of two large white lion statues perched on the rooftop of an ornate stone building against a starry night sky. Between them stands a girl in a bright pink dress, reaching toward one of the lions, with a small tabby cat sitting on the ledge below and a few tiny colorful creatures nearby. A sculpted face relief decorates the building's facade.
history: This illustration by Latvian artist Anita Paegle is titled The Smile of the Alberta Sphinx ("Sfinksas Albertas smaids"). Created with delicate watercolors, the artwork reimagines the iconic Art Nouveau (Jūgendstils) architectural heritage of Riga, Latvia, transforming the real-world stone lions and expressive facade sculptures found on historic Alberta Street into whimsical characters under a starry night sky.

title: Bondegård
description: A vibrant, cartoonish farm landscape set against a rich teal backdrop with thick, bold black outlines. A cheerful mix of animals—including a blue dog, pink pigs, a smiling horse, red cows, and white sheep—surround two white houses with bright red roofs flying a Danish flag.
history: Created by celebrated Danish artist Bo Bendixen (studio founded in 1973), this piece exemplifies modern Scandinavian graphic design. Known for his joyful optimism and minimalist forms, Bendixen captures the idealized Danish countryside (det danske landskab). His iconic style combines pop-art simplicity with Nordic motifs, making his posters a staple of late 20th-century Danish culture and home decor.

title: The land of the midnight sun
description: Illustrated, colorful map of Norway set against a white background, filled with playful drawings of landmarks and wildlife. The cursive title "The land of the midnight sun" sits in the top-left corner, while "Norway" is written in large text at the bottom right. The map features polar bears in the north, an elk in the center, and whales in the surrounding blue ocean. Major cities like Oslo, Bergen, and Trondheim are marked with sketches of historic buildings, alongside a small block of handwritten factual data about the country.
history: This piece is a classic mid-to-late 20th-century souvenir postcard designed for the Norwegian tourism boom. It highlights core pillars of Norway's national identity: its rich Viking heritage, its modern maritime economy (symbolized by the offshore oil rig), and its breathtaking Arctic geography. The famous moniker "The Land of the Midnight Sun" celebrates the unique natural phenomenon occurring north of the Arctic Circle during summer, which remains a primary global attraction for travelers.

title: Blades from Momoyogusa
description: A traditional Japanese woodblock print composed of diagonal, overlapping rectangular strips overlaid on a tan textured background. Each strip contains stylized figures rendered with black line work, flat colors like green, yellow, and black, and expressive facial features characteristic of classical Japanese illustration. In the upper right corner, a small, circular red artist's seal is stamped onto the background.
history: This image is a woodblock print by the renowned Japanese artist Kamisaka Sekka (1866-1942) from his famous multi-volume masterwork Momoyogusa (Flowers of a Hundred Worlds), published in 1909. Sekka was the leading figure of the early 20th-century revival of the Rinpa school, an artistic style that emphasized stylized natural motifs, literature-inspired subjects, and innovative graphic layouts. This specific composition uses a distinct narrative framing technique reminiscent of traditional emaki (handscrolls), creating a dynamic visual rhythm that bridges traditional Edo-period aesthetics with early modern design.

title: Children of the Forest
description: A whimsical watercolor illustration depicting a family of miniature forest children harvesting wild goods in a lush green clearing. The children are dressed in simple light tunics, and most wear bright red hats with white spots resembling amanita mushrooms. One woman in a white dress carries a large basket overflowing with red berries, while small children carry enormous mushrooms—including a bright yellow chanterelle. In the background, a figure with a pinecone head works with a small axe near towering, realistic wild mushrooms and green moss.
history: This image is a classic illustration by the famous Swedish author and illustrator Elsa Beskow (1874–1953), taken from her beloved 1910 children's book Tomtebobarnen (Children of the Forest). Beskow is a cornerstone of Nordic children's literature, renowned for her ability to weave contemporary Art Nouveau styling with traditional Swedish folklore. Her work deeply reflects the Scandinavian cultural love for nature and the countryside, reimagining the forest floor as a magical, harmonious community. Postcards featuring her artwork have been widely collected across Europe for over a century, celebrating nostalgic, idyllic themes of childhood and the changing seasons.

title: Bauta
description: Detailed watercolor illustration of an anthropomorphic tabby cat dressed in a historical Italian costume against a plain white background. The cat wears a sweeping brown and gold cloak (tabarro), a dark hood framing its feline face, and a long red coat accented with structured button details. In one paw, it holds up a traditional white Carnival mask, while a black tricorn hat (tricorno) is tucked under its arm. Elegant script at the bottom reads "Bauta - Firenze".
history: It features a contemporary artistic rendering that celebrates classic Italian theatrical and festive traditions. The attire depicted is the Bauta, one of the most famous and historically significant disguises of the Venetian Carnival, widely worn during the 17th and 18th centuries. The ensemble was designed specifically to grant total anonymity across social classes, featuring a unique white mask (larva) shaped to let the wearer eat and talk without removing it. While the costume itself is iconic to Venice, the inscription "Firenze" (Florence) indicates its place within a broader regional art collection celebrating the historical pageantry and Commedia dell'Arte heritage of Italy. By Susan Hebert.

title: Bunny Food - Taiwan Street Food
description: Textured illustration showcasing an array of Taiwanese street food delicacies reimagined with adorable animal faces. In the center, a clear cup of boba milk tea features tapioca pearls shaped like tiny black rabbits. Surrounding the drink are various treats: a wheel cake (imagawayaki) cut open to reveal a sweet red bean filling with eyes, a bag of golden sweet potato balls shaped like bunnies, a piece of crispy Taiwanese fried chicken with a cat-like face, and a glossy, red strawberry tanghulu skewer on the left. The artwork uses warm, grainy textures and soft earth tones.
history: This postcard features the work of ririkoko 梨々子々, an independent Taiwanese digital illustrator known for blending culinary art with animal motifs. The brand name ririkoko is a playful phonetic translation of the Taiwanese Hokkien phrase li-li-khou-khou (哩哩摳摳), which means "many small, miscellaneous things"—reflecting the artist's love for small daily joys and miniature collectibles. By infusing iconic Taiwanese night market treats with a distinct contemporary kawaii (cute) aesthetic, ririkoko's work epitomizes a popular 21st-century movement among young Taiwanese designers who use comforting, whimsical illustrations to celebrate, preserve, and globally export local street food heritage

title: Lovely Day for a Guinness
description: Vintage-style advertisement poster for the Irish stout brand Guinness, set against an off-white background with a dark green border. In the center, a cartoon green tortoise walks toward the right, carefully balancing an enormous, full pint glass of dark Guinness beer with a thick, frothy white head on top of its shell. At the top of the poster, the iconic slogan "Lovely day for a GUINNESS" is printed in bold red letters, with "GUINNESS" appearing in a much larger font. At the very bottom, the word "IRELAND" is written in a stylized, historic Celtic-style black font.
history: One of the most famous and enduring advertisement campaigns in brewing history, originally created by the illustrator John Gilroy for the S.H. Benson advertising agency in the 1930s. Gilroy’s iconic zoo animal series—which famously included a tortoise, a toucan, a sea lion, and a kangaroo—revolutionized commercial illustration by injecting humor, vivid color, and whimsical narratives into a brand that had previously relied on more conservative layouts. The turtle balancing a pint was playfully used to represent the slow, meticulous patience required to perfectly pour a pint of Guinness stout, turning a potential consumer drawback into a beloved cultural trademark. Today, these vintage illustrations remain powerful symbols of Irish pub culture, heritage, and international nostalgia.

title: Prospect of Rosenborg Castle in the time of Christian VI
description: Depicting the symmetrical facade of Rosenborg Castle in Copenhagen, viewed from an elevated perspective across the expansive King's Garden (Kongens Have). The three-story Dutch Renaissance palace stands centrally with its iconic soaring spires, surrounded by meticulously manicured Baroque hedge gardens, gravel pathways, and small water fountains where figures in 17th- or 18th-century period clothing stroll. Heavy, lush green tree canopies frame the lower foreground, while windmills dot the soft green hills rolling toward the horizon under a pale, cloudy sky.
history: Historic painting—specifically a famous 18th-century gouache projection—capturing Rosenborg Castle and its royal pleasure gardens during its architectural golden age. Built between 1606 and 1634 by King Christian IV as a summer residence, the castle is a prime example of Dutch Renaissance architecture in Scandinavia. The elaborate formal gardens showcased here, originally laid out before the castle itself, reflect the absolute monarchy's transition toward Baroque aesthetic ideals of symmetry and human dominance over nature. As a postcard artifact, this piece highlights Denmark’s deep-seated pride in its royal lineage, preservation of its green urban heritage (Kongens Have remains the oldest royal garden in the country), and classic European landscape art traditions.

title: Longshan Temple
store: CKS Memorial Hall Museum Gift Shop
description: Vintage-style textured illustration depicting the grand frontal facade of a traditional Taiwanese temple against a plain white background. The structure features a striking sweeping orange-tiled roof with dramatic upturned eaves decorated with detailed carvings of dragons and phoenixes. The ornate wooden facade includes gold-accented pillars, hanging red lanterns, and small oval window niches on the sides displaying Buddha statues. In front of the entrance sit two potted bonsai trees and a central bronze incense burner. At the bottom, text in black reads "寺廟 ． 台灣" (Temple ． Taiwan), followed by "Temple" in English and "お寺" in Japanese.
history: The iconic Bangka Longshan Temple in Taipei, Taiwan. Originally built in 1738 by immigrants from Fujian, China, it stands as one of Taiwan's oldest and most architecturally significant spiritual landmarks. The design showcases classical Southern Chinese (Minnan) temple architecture, famous for its swallow-tail ridged roofs and intricate multi-layered woodcarvings. Serving as a multi-denominational hub where Buddhist, Taoist, and folk deities like Mazu are worshipped together, the temple represents the core of Taipei’s community history and religious resilience. Postcards featuring tri-lingual text (Chinese, English, and Japanese) became popular in the mid-to-late 20th century to cater to international heritage tourists.

title: Embankment Place
description: Textured pointillism illustration closely framing the geometric, industrial details of a modern London architectural structure. The composition highlights a cylindrical glass tower with teal-green metal framing and ventilation grilles, contrasted against a massive, white three-dimensional steel truss framework in the background. In the top left corner, the text reads "London's new architecture by bus and tube," accompanied by the iconic red roundel logo of London Transport in the top right.
history: This postcard reproduces a celebrated art poster commissioned by London Transport in 1996, created by the acclaimed printmaker Edwina Ellis. The image is part of a series of intricate multiblock color wood engravings capturing the dramatic rise of postmodern and High-Tech architecture in London. This specific panel depicts a detailed close-up of Embankment Place, the famous complex built over Charing Cross station designed by Terry Farrell. Ellis’s work continues London Transport's world-renowned legacy of employing avant-garde artists to turn public transit marketing into prized pieces of modern graphic design history.

title: Ostrovy, Praha
description: Detailed, outline drawing showcasing a panoramic, bird's-eye view of an urban waterfront landscape. Intricate pen strokes depict dense rows of historic, multi-story European buildings at both the top and bottom edges, framing a wide body of water in the center. The water features small islands covered in rounded, cloud-like trees, a few small boats with figures, and minimal wavy lines to indicate ripples.
history: Illustration by Hungarian artist Balázs Egri captures the distinct architectural identity of Budapest, Hungary, blending elements from the historic sides of Buda and Peste. The crowded, ornate facades reflect the late 19th-century boom of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, a period characterized by Eclectic, Neo-Renaissance, and Art Nouveau styles. By depicting public parks, riverboats, and dense promenades, the artwork celebrates Central Europe's enduring café culture and vibrant urban riverfront life.

title: Rain or Shine Tiger
store: 來好 LAI HAO 永康本店
description: Vibrant, whimsical illustration features a stylized white tiger covered in bold yellow and black stripes, walking across a bright blue background. Above the tiger are a smiling yellow sun with rays and a grumpy black rain cloud with a sad face, while a small black cat walks beside the tiger's paws and Chinese characters adorn the upper left and bottom right corners.
history: Created by the Hong Kong-based design studio All Things Bright And Beautiful, the artwork's handwritten Chinese calligraphy deeply enriches its visual narrative by introducing profound themes of emotional coexistence and shared resilience. The phrases "有苦，有樂" ("there is bitterness, there is joy") and the Cantonese-inflected "一齊行" ("let's walk this journey together") act as a direct philosophical commentary on the image. By placing these words alongside a whimsical tiger simultaneously bathed in golden sunshine and dynamic rain streaks, the studio masterfully utilizes its signature lighthearted, story-driven artistic style to explore the duality of the human experience. Ultimately, it serves as a comforting reminder of balance and harmony, illustrating that life's hardships and blessings always run parallel, and that navigating these contrasting conditions becomes meaningful through community and companionship.

title: Poster for the Zurich Tourist Office
description: Vintage travel poster features an impressionistic painting of a lively lakeside promenade in Zurich, filled with stylishly dressed pedestrians and docked sailboats. In the background, a steamboat billows smoke under a blue sky, while snow-capped mountains frame the distant horizon above the bold, dark blue "ZURICH" lettering at the bottom.
history: Created in 1916 by the Swiss artist Otto Baumberger, during the early 20th century, this artwork exemplifies the golden age of Swiss travel poster design, which used romanticized, artistic imagery to promote tourism. Posters like this were instrumental in positioning Switzerland—and Zurich specifically—as an accessible, culturally vibrant, and scenic destination for international travelers via expanding rail and steamship networks.

title: Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok
description: Watercolor illustration features a wide view of a grand, weathered stone facade set against a clear blue sky, with a sloping green lawn and scattered figures in the foreground. A distinct zigzag path cuts through the lawn, and Chinese characters reading "澳門大三巴" appear in the bottom right corner.
history: This artwork captures the iconic urban landscape and bustling transit system of Hong Kong, specifically highlighting its characteristic red-top public light buses navigating the dense high-rise environment. Such scenes reflect the energetic pace and distinct architectural density that define the city's vibrant street life.

title: L'Assedio di Firenze
description: High-angle, panoramic landscape painting depicts a sprawling Renaissance city encircled by a river and green hills, with an active military encampment and tents covering the foreground. A seated allegorical figure is visible in the lower left corner, while the background reveals distant mountains under an overcast sky.
history: Painted by Giorgio Vasari between 1556 and 1562 in the Palazzo Vecchio, this fresco commemorates the historic Siege of Florence from 1529 to 1530. The artwork captures the pivotal military conflict where Imperial and papal forces blockaded the Florentine Republic, ultimately restoring the rule of the Medici family.

title: Ruins of St. Paul's, Macao
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte
description: Watercolor illustration features a wide view of a grand, weathered stone facade set against a clear blue sky, with a sloping green lawn and scattered figures in the foreground. A distinct zigzag path cuts through the lawn, and Chinese characters reading "澳門大三巴" appear in the bottom right corner.
history: This artwork depicts the Ruins of St. Paul's (Ruínas de São Paulo), a 17th-century Catholic complex in Macau dedicated to Saint Paul and originally built by the Jesuits. Today, the iconic stone façade—surviving after a catastrophic fire in 1835—stands as one of Macau's most famous historic landmarks and a symbol of the region's unique Portuguese and Chinese cultural heritage.

title: Calcifer's Bacon and Eggs
description: Hand-drawn animation still features a frying pan sizzling with thick-cut bacon and three sunny-side-up eggs, placed directly over an animated fire spirit with a wide-eyed, expressive face. The glowing, fiery base of the pan is surrounded by small, dark stone figures, creating a warm, stylized scene.
history: This iconic scene comes from Studio Ghibli's 2004 animated fantasy film Howl's Moving Castle, directed by Hayao Miyazaki. The fiery creature is Calcifer, a bound fire demon who dramatically and enthusiastically cooks breakfast for the characters using his own magical flame.

title: The Golden Dragon
store: CKS Memorial Hall Museum Gift Shop
description: This detailed close-up illustration depicts a golden Chinese imperial dragon with intricate scales, long white whiskers, a pink snout, and a wide-open red mouth, framed against a pale, patterned background. Below its head, the dragon's coiled body loops around a central flaming pearl motif, surrounded by stylized clouds and stylized claw details.
history: In traditional Chinese culture and art, the golden five-clawed dragon is a powerful symbol of imperial authority, nobility, and good fortune, historically reserved exclusively for the Emperor. This imagery reflects centuries of royal symbolism where the dragon chasing the flaming pearl represented wisdom, spiritual energy, and prosperity.

title: In the Shade
description: High-angle, whimsical mixed-media painting of a pale-walled, dark-roofed cottage nestled within a vibrant green and yellow forest. In the foreground, a textured meadow glows with expressive daubs of yellow and pink, while dark, dense tree canopies frame the secluded house from above.

title: A Casa de Chá de Ichikiri
Guinness Heritage Extra Stout Label
description: vertical, oval-shaped product label design features a vibrant orange-yellow background enclosed within a black rectangular frame, centered on a harp graphic, bold black typography reading "GUINNESS EXTRA STOUT ST. JAMES'S GATE DUBLIN", a red signature, and the word "IRELAND" at the bottom.
history: This historic label represents Guinness Extra Stout, brewed at the iconic St. James's Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland, established by Arthur Guinness in 1759. The design incorporates the legendary Guinness harp—a symbol inspired by the ancient "Brian Boru" harp—serving as a globally recognized emblem of Irish heritage and brewing tradition.
